newsitem.title: USA: Federal grand jury indicts Missouri power brokers.
newsitem.headline: Federal grand jury indicts Missouri power brokers.

text.p: A federal grand jury on Thursday indicted some of Missouri's leading power brokers in one of the most far-reaching public corruption probes in state history, prosecutors said.

Among those indicted on federal bribery and racketeering charges were former Missouri House Speaker Bob Griffin. Others charged in the 26-count indictment were Mike Fisher, a labor leader in Kansas City and Cathryn Simmons, a veteran political consultant.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Bruce Clark said the indictment alleges that from 1992 to 1994, the defendants engaged in a series of schemes that involved paying bribes to Griffin and one other man in order to illegally influence the operation of Missouri government.
Joining prosecutors in announcing the indictment was a special agent from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, which conducted a 27-month criminal investigation that led to the indictments.
If convicted, Griffin could be sentenced to a maximum 90 years in prison without parole and could be ordered to pay as much as $2.25 million in fines.
Griffin, Simmons and Fisher have all denied wrongdoing.
